appraisal_events.evidence: « Mais prenez-la donc, voilà une heure que je vous la passe » ; « On ne joue pas quand on ne veut pas faire attention et pour faire perdre les autres. On ne l'invitera plus les jours où on jouera » ; le narrateur reste « Étourdi de chagrin », « désespéré », « interpellé par les moqueries de toutes les joueuses ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's elaborate maneuver to sit beside Albertine culminates in his misreading her hand-pressure and wink as a private avowal of love; Albertine's angry public correction, backed by the mockery of the whole group and her threat to have him excluded from future games, collapses that imagined intimacy into humiliation, and the narrator stages the fall himself.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Andrée gardait le flegme souriant d'un dandy femelle » face à Albertine qui « suait à grosses gouttes » ; elle impose ses critiques (« il faut surtout citer Deltour et Gascq-Desfossés »), reste « supérieure au jeu », s'adresse au narrateur « avec un sourire du regard qui n'était que pour moi », puis le conduit aux Creuniers « avec une divination charmante ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Across the passage Andrée is consistently placed above the others — intellectually over an awed Albertine, socially above the game, and in a flattering private complicity with the narrator whom she alone consoles — but the narrator qualifies the elevation with irony (the « dandy femelle », the Trianon comparison, her singing « sans en avoir envie », her refusal to give Albertine the titles she begs for).

status_effects.explanation: He falls from « au comble d'une joie » at the imagined avowal to being « Étourdi de chagrin » and « désespéré », his hoped-for leverage over Albertine revealed as pure self-delusion.

He is sent back to the middle of the circle, jeered at by all the players, and explicitly threatened with disinvitation from the group's games, though Andrée's walk to the Creuniers softens the exclusion.
She gains local leverage: radiant and unconcerned, she dictates the group's judgment of the narrator and can grant or withhold the intimacy he has organized his whole afternoon around.

She is locally raised as the poised, cultivated, tactful member of the band — above the schoolgirl game and its quarrels — even though the narrator lets her poise show a faint streak of vanity and withholding.

ambiguities: Albertine's hand-pressure, caressing finger and wink are genuinely underdetermined: the narrator reads them as « Elle profite du jeu pour me faire sentir qu'elle m'aime bien », her immediate rage reframes them as game tactics, and the text does not settle whether her rebuke is a snub or mere impatience — which affects how sharply E1 should be read as an evaluative act by her rather than a purely self-inflicted disappointment.

Andrée's elevation is carried by the narrator's own admiring perception while being simultaneously ironized (the « dandy femelle », the Trianon-fête comparison, her deliberate refusal to give Albertine the critics' names), so it is unclear how far the passage endorses her superiority rather than exhibiting her performance of it.
